resources.string: Your private identity is ready. It lives only on this phone, locked by your PIN. No account, no phone number, no server knows who you are.
Your PIN is the only key
You just chose a PIN. It is the ONLY way in — there is no reset and no recovery. If you forget it, your data is gone for good. Tip: typing your PIN backwards is the panic wipe (the Shredder).

The Engine connects you over the Tor network. \"Online\" means friends can reach you. \"Invisible\" means you still receive messages but look offline to everyone. You always start Invisible — switch from the main screen when you\'re ready.
Add a friend with a QR code
Tap the cyan + on the Friends screen and choose Add friend. Show your QR code or scan your friend\'s. You each add the other once — after that you can message privately.

The red power symbol (Exit) clears everything from memory and logs you out. \"Wipe Everything\" in Settings deletes all data on this phone. And remember: your PIN typed backwards instantly and silently wipes everything.

They get a friend request (even if they\'re Invisible or their app is closed). Until they accept they show as \"New Friend\" (or your nickname for them); then the name they chose — unless you gave them one. Tap a waiting friend to cancel.
Your ID appears once Tor is Online and your server is published.
⚠ v0.1 is test software. It has not had an independent security audit and is for trying things out with friends — not for real-life safety or high-risk use.

Please read this before you rely on CM-Chat.

1. CM-Chat is peer-to-peer over Tor. There is no server, no account, and no one who can recover your data or your PIN for you. If you forget your PIN, your data is gone — by design.

2. Both phones must be connected at the same time for a message to move. There is no server mailbox: your phone keeps re-sending until your friend's phone confirms it has the message.

3. Messages live only in memory and are erased when you wipe or Exit. One exception: a message that arrives while CM-Chat is locked or closed is kept on the phone sealed (encrypted to your identity key) until your next unlock, then shown and shredded. Apart from that, only the encrypted vault (your identity, friends and settings) is written to disk.

4. Your safety depends on your device. If your phone is unlocked, compromised, or taken while open, CM-Chat cannot protect you. Use the screen lock, Cerberus idle-wipe, the Kill Timer, and the reverse-PIN shredder.

5. Metadata still matters. Tor hides the network path, but who you talk to, when, and how often can still be inferred by someone watching you in person or holding your device. Invisible mode, buzz throttling and coarse last-seen reduce — not eliminate — this.

6. This is test software. Do not use it where being discovered would put you or anyone else at risk. Treat every build as experimental until an independent security audit says otherwise.

Stay careful. Trust your own judgement over any app.
Used memory over time, labelled by active features. Separate from the Tor log.

This is your app\'s signing fingerprint. Compare it with a friend (read it aloud or scan): if they match, you\'re both running the genuine, unmodified CM-Chat. A different fingerprint means a repackaged or tampered build.

Makes your Tor traffic look like normal web traffic, so your network can\'t tell you use Tor. Can be slower. It does NOT add message secrecy — your messages are already end-to-end encrypted either way.
Disguise Tor as random traffic. Most reliable bridge type.
Route via volunteer browser proxies. Experimental here.
Your own bridge lines (one per line)
Custom bridges are more reliable long-term than the built-in ones. Get them from Tor (bridges.torproject.org) or a friend. Leave blank to use the built-in fallback set.
If bridges are on and can\'t connect, the app will NOT fall back to normal Tor — it shows \"Failed (bridges)\" instead, so your cloak is never bypassed.
Sends decoy traffic to hide when you\'re really messaging. Uses more battery and data.

No connection activity yet. Run a Link Test, or send/receive a message.

Rotates to a fresh onion and tells your contacts; the old address stays alive ~24h so no one drops.

It\'s the only key — there is NO reset and NO recovery. Use 4 to 56 characters: numbers, letters or symbols; 8 or more is much stronger. It can\'t read the same backwards, because your PIN typed backwards is the Shredder.
Connects you over the Tor network. The first start can take 1–3 minutes. If your Wi-Fi or mobile data drops for a moment, it reconnects by itself and keeps your address.
Your nickname is what friends see when you add them (change it in Settings → My nickname). Your address (CMC-ID) and QR code are in Settings → My identity: show, copy or share them there.

Tap the cyan + and choose Add friend. Scan their QR (or paste their CMC-ID), add a nickname for them if you like, and tap Add friend. Until they accept they show as \"New Friend\" (or your nickname for them) with \"Pending\" — tap the row to cancel the request or remove them. Only ONE of you needs to add the other. It keeps trying quietly until their phone confirms.

A friend request arrives as a card on the Friends screen — Accept or Decline. It gets through even while you\'re Invisible or the app is closed. A declined person can\'t send another for an hour. Once accepted, you see the nickname they chose (your own label for them, if you set one, wins).
Everything happens on the phone. The camera is only used while you\'re scanning.

Every message gets brand-new one-time keys, so even someone who later steals the phone and its keys can\'t read messages they recorded earlier (forward secrecy). Nothing on screen shows delivered or read. If your friend is offline, the message waits quietly and is re-sent until their phone confirms it has it (while your app is running). Each message shows the time it was sent or received (like 4:05 PM).

Tap the paperclip left of the message box. Up to 100 MB. Photos and videos have their location and camera data removed before they leave; if that can\'t be done, the file is not sent. Other files go exactly as they are (documents can hold their own hidden data). Received files stay in memory only, are never opened by the app, and disappear with the chat — tap Save to keep one.

Tap a choice in the 🔥 bar above the message box: Off, Single Message (view once — gone the moment it\'s read), or a time (30s up to 24h) after it\'s seen. The 🔥 pill at the top shows what your next message gets. A timer for ALL messages is in Settings → Chats.

A shared clock for one chat — handy for agreeing on a time. Tap \"Set Team Clock\" in the chat and set the time like a phone alarm; both of you see it. It survives both phones restarting, and the newest change wins.

A nudge with no text: long-press a friend, or ⚡ Buzz in the chat. Their phone shows a notification, and a BLUE dot stays on your name until they open your chat. It reaches them even when their app is closed. Settings → Chats → Accept Buzz limits how often anyone can Buzz you.
The red X in a chat
Wipe conversation: erases it on BOTH phones (theirs as soon as it reaches them). Delete friend: removes them from your list on this phone. Each one asks you to confirm.

Every time the app starts (and after Exit) you\'re Invisible. Tap your status (● Online / ● Invisible) on the Friends screen to switch — only your tap changes it; minimising keeps your choice. Invisible = you still receive, but look offline: no notifications for messages (a Buzz, a friend request or a friend\'s decoy alert still notifies), and they wait as \"Missed Message\". Go Online and they\'re delivered as new messages. Senders can\'t tell.

Swiping the app away keeps the Engine listening. A Buzz notifies you. Messages that arrive are kept on the phone sealed (encrypted to your identity key), never readable without your PIN, and show as \"Missed Message\" after you unlock — then they\'re shredded from storage. Exit ends all of this.
A blue dot on a friend means a new message is waiting. It goes away when you open that chat while Online. There is no \"online\" dot — nobody\'s status is shown.
Friends only ever see \"last seen recently\" — for a day after you last sent them something, even if you then go Invisible or close the app.
The white line minimises: the Engine keeps running. The red power symbol exits: it stops everything, clears memory (your keys too) and logs you out.
Sensitive settings (server, stealth, guardians, PIN, wipe, diagnostics) can sit behind a separate Privacy PIN (digits only). You can change it or remove it.
Idle auto-wipe: if the app goes untouched for the time you choose (15 min–3 h), it clears memory, stops the Engine and closes. Your vault stays.
Set it like an alarm (the time it goes off); then it does the same as Cerberus.

A fake friend. Tapping it instantly wipes your chats from memory, moves you to a new address and locks the app. It also sends a burn signal: each confirmed friend who is online gets your chat wiped on their phone too and sees \"Decoy chat triggered — chat erased.\"

Settings → Privacy & Safety → Open as a calculator: the app opens to a working calculator. Tap the same key 10 times in a row to get in (the first time, that key becomes yours). Tap \"reset\" 20 times to choose a different key. Your PIN still guards everything.

Type your PIN BACKWARDS at the lock screen: everything is silently erased and a small red \"Error. Please restart the app.\" appears under \"Welcome back\". Close and reopen the app and it starts fresh (no reinstall needed).
Settings → Privacy & Safety. Erases all app data, then opens Android\'s uninstall prompt so the app itself can be removed too.
Bridges hide from your network that you use Tor (slower). Cover traffic sends decoy traffic so nobody can tell when you really message (more battery).
Settings → Connection test runs a Link Test to one friend and shows every step live, on both phones — the best way to see where a connection fails.
If you see this, you and a friend run different app versions. Install the same version on both phones.
Diagnostics shows what the app is doing; the self-test checks its own defences; Verify App Integrity shows the app\'s signing fingerprint to compare with a friend.
